title: My Decisions and Habits This Year
writingModel: Decisions, Habits, and Hopes: My Year So Far — by Rustam Seilov

This year I have tried to be more intentional about how I spend my time. I used to drift from task to task, putting off important things and hoping they would somehow complete themselves. That approach stopped working some time around November. So I made some decisions.

The first was to give up checking social media in the evenings. I had been spending hours scrolling without really enjoying it — just doing it out of habit. I decided to stop, and for the first two weeks I genuinely missed it. By the third week I had forgotten why I bothered. I have started reading instead, and I enjoy it far more. Currently I am reading a biography of Abai, which I would recommend to anyone who is interested in Kazakh literature.

The second decision was to start exercising three times a week. I had been avoiding exercise for most of the year, telling myself I was too busy. That was partly true and partly an excuse. I promised myself to stop making excuses and just begin. I am now in my fifth week, and I have managed to keep the habit going. I don't always enjoy the exercise itself — I particularly dislike running — but I enjoy having done it. That is enough motivation.

The third change is about studying. I tend to work in long, unstructured sessions which are not particularly effective. I have decided to try studying in shorter, more focused blocks of time. I have been practising this technique for three weeks. I cannot yet say whether it is working, but I intend to continue and see.

There are some habits I am still struggling to change. I keep forgetting to drink enough water. I keep putting off calling my grandmother, even though I always enjoy talking to her once I do. These are small things, but I consider keeping up small habits to be as important as the big decisions.

My hope for the end of the year is to look back and feel that I used this semester well — that I made good decisions, kept my promises to myself, and didn't avoid the things that were difficult. That is my plan. I intend to keep working at it.
